Does she A, want vengeance? B, become depressed? C, fall in love with one of the guys? She becomes depressed or she falls in love. It's often the case that she falls in love. This is known as the Stockholm syndrome—a basic human psychology consistent throughout history and all societies. When a woman sees her entire life collapse, she has no stability; her reality is destroyed, leading her to cling to anyone who supports her, even if that person destroyed her life initially.

So, A, do they feel guilty for what they do? B, do they fight over the woman? Or C, are they brothers forever? They're brothers forever. Even though they commit a terrible act, it unifies them more.

The structure of secret societies involves people at the top committing rituals to turn initiates into slaves. Those most willing to participate become middlepeople and trusted individuals because now they are slaves. Secret societies have different degrees; at the very top, no one knows what is really happening—they pray to Satan or Saturn for strength to torture initiates, turning them into lifelong slaves with limitless wealth and power.

In Sparta, Spartans maintain control over their helots (slaves) by being cohesive as a society. At age 5 or 6, Spartan children are taken from parents, creating fear and anxiety. They experience trauma when beaten by older kids in school. Around ages 11 or 12, boys are paired with older men who become lovers; despite abuse, the boy falls in love due to his lack of reality and support, doing anything ordered by the man.
